topic: The Arctic Tern Migrates About 70,000 Kilometers Each Year, the Longest Animal Migration
title: This 100g Bird Flies 70,000km Every Single Year
description: A 100-gram bird flies 70,000km every year. That's 2.4 million km in a lifetime. Professor Croc breaks down the fat tank, the quantum magnetic compass, and the wind hack that makes the longest migration on Earth possible.
staircase: Earth is tilted 23.5 degrees, so the poles flip between 24-hour sun and 24-hour darkness.
That flip creates a moving buffet of summer where plankton doubles every 24 hours under constant sun.
That bloom pulls fish and krill into the top 2 meters, concentrating calories where a 4-centimeter beak can reach.
That calorie density is converted to fat at 8 kilocalories per gram, building a 40-gram fuel tank on a 100-gram bird.
That fuel tank powers pectoral muscles beating 35 times per second to sustain 10 meters per second while burning 8x resting metabolism.
That 10 meters per second held for 8 hours a day for 240 travel days adds up to 70,000 kilometers per year.
To survive 70,000 kilometers over empty ocean, it reads Earth's 25 to 65 microtesla magnetic field with magnetite and cryptochrome in its retina.
That magnetic compass is corrected by a time-compensated sun compass that adjusts 15 degrees per hour with its internal clock.
Those two compasses combined create a figure-eight route that rides 30 to 50 kilometer per hour westerlies to save 20% energy.
That 20% saving repeated over a 30-year lifespan totals 2.4 million kilometers, equal to three round trips to the Moon.
thumbnail_prompt: A tiny arctic tern in mid-flight beside planet Earth with a thin line wrapping pole to pole around the globe showing its migration route
extra_credit: It lives in 2 summers per year and sees more daylight than any other animal on Earth - about 8 months of pure daylight annually.
